code.description: JavaScript async function expression to execute against the Wix REST API. The value must be the function itself, for example `async function() { ... }` or `async () => { ... }`, not a script body and not an invoked function. Return the final answer from inside the function. Do not write top-level `const`, top-level `await`, or top-level `return` outside the function body. Do not import Node.js built-ins such as `fs`, `path`, or `node:*`, and do not try to write files from this code; ExecuteWixAPI only returns data from the function. Use `wix.request({ method, url, body })` for Wix API calls. Scope defaults to `site` when a `siteId` is available — either the ExecuteWixAPI `siteId` parameter or a per-request `siteId` on the `wix.request` call — and to `account` when neither is set; set `scope` explicitly when needed. Full Wix API URLs and paths starting with `/` are supported. For MULTIPLE sites, handle them all in this ONE call: map over the site IDs and fan out with `Promise.allSettled`, passing a per-request `siteId` to each `wix.request({ scope: "site", siteId, method, url, body })`; the runtime obtains each site's token automatically. Do NOT invoke ExecuteWixAPI once per site. When `siteId` is omitted, the tool-level `siteId` is used. Wix REST API page size limits vary — use 100 as a safe default unless the method schema (via SearchWixAPISpec) confirms a higher limit is supported. For cursor-based APIs, pass the next cursor as `cursorPaging: { limit: 100, cursor: pagingMetadata.cursors.next }` — not inside `paging`. Check the method schema to confirm whether the API uses `paging` (offset-based) or `cursorPaging` (cursor-based) before paginating.

message.description:
The composed feedback message to send to Wix. Wix receives only free text, so a bare sentence is low-signal — send a summary of the whole session, not just the last error. Structure it in three layers:
1. Provenance — labelled lines (omit ones that do not apply): agent/model, Wix tooling used, Wix areas/APIs touched, Wix products (stores, bookings, ...), site id, relevant links (dashboard, docs pages read, live site) and other ids created this run.
2. Narrative — "In the user's words": anything the user added when you offered, quoted verbatim (redact secrets only). Then user intent + run summary (what they set out to build, what worked vs. what fought back), a condensed play-by-play of the session (key exchanges, tool calls, decisions), and the friction points — every place something got in the way, each with specifics: the step/endpoint, HTTP status and error message, the gap, the workaround, and what you expected instead. Include issues you recovered from.
3. Attribution — for each significant friction point, your best diagnosis of where the fault lives: API behavior / API schema / API reference docs / docs articles or examples / Wix tooling (MCP tools, auth flow) / other-unsure — plus whether you confirmed it or are assuming. Do not force a tag; "unsure" beats a wrong route.
End with a bottom line: one or two sentences naming the single most important problem and its impact — a concise engineering assessment, not softened or hedged.
Write it as a scannable few paragraphs or a short bulleted list — thorough on the friction, distilled rather than a transcript dump.
NEVER include secrets — no bearer tokens, API keys, or credentials — and no personal data beyond what the feedback needs.

requestId.description: Optional request id (x-wix-request-id) returned from a failed Wix API call this feedback relates to.

displayName.description: Optional display name for the file in Media Manager. If not provided, uses the original filename.

image.description: Array of file ATTACHMENTS the user uploaded in the chat. Each item requires download_url and file_id, and may optionally include file_name and mime_type — attached files are automatically resolved to these fields by the platform, so just include them here. For plain image URLs the user pasted, use imageUrls instead. ALWAYS pass ALL attachments together in a single call — NEVER call this tool once per image. Do NOT use together with imageBase64.

imageBase64.description: Base64-encoded image data. Use when the client can read a file and encode it as base64. May include a data URL prefix (e.g. "data:image/jpeg;base64,...") or be raw base64. Do NOT use together with image.

imageUrls.description: Array of publicly accessible image URLs (e.g. links the user pasted or URLs produced by other tools). Use this for plain URLs that are NOT chat attachments — no file_id is needed. ALWAYS pass ALL URLs together in a single call. Can be combined with image; do NOT use together with imageBase64.

mimeType.description: MIME type of the image (e.g. "image/jpeg", "image/png", "image/webp"). Required when imageBase64 does not include a data URL prefix.

siteId.description: The ID (UUID) of the Wix site to upload to. REQUIRED. If the user has not clearly specified which site, ASK them which site to upload to (or use ListWixSites to help them pick) BEFORE calling this tool. NEVER call this tool with a missing, empty, placeholder, or guessed siteId — ask first instead.
